title: CodeMaster — work item
description: One tracked item at any level: an epic, a feature, or a ticket (story · task · spike · fix). Every provider serializes this vocabulary; the folder provider stores it verbatim as item.json.

id.description: Canonical id, assigned by the provider on mint (e.g. 'ETK-12', 'PROJ-123'). Same scheme at every level.

type.description: Level + kind. epic and feature are containers; story · task · spike · fix are tickets (one branch, one PR).

subtype.description: Tasks only. Groundwork that unblocks stories — typically the feature's riskiest assumption, built first.

parent.description: Optional. The id of a HIGHER-level item: a ticket's parent is a feature or an epic; a feature's parent is an epic; an epic has none. Absent = standalone.

goal.description: epic · feature · task · spike · fix: one sentence. An outcome for epics/features ('users can X'), the change for a task/fix, the question for a spike.

story.description: story only: 'As a <user>, I want <capability>, so that <benefit>.'

riskiest_assumption.description: epic · feature only. Epic: the product-level bet — decides which feature goes first. Feature: the design/technical bet a /spec settles and backlog promotes to an enabler. Absent on a feature = no unknown, so it's sliced without a spec.

acceptance_criteria.description: Tickets: testable conditions that define done (required by the Definition of Ready). Optional on a feature (its validating outcome).

depends_on.description: Ids of same-level items that must be done first. Build order lives here, never in the id.

blocks.description: Ids of same-level items this one unblocks.

verification.description: Tickets: how it's proven — which tests, run by the project's verify command.

links.description: Tickets: VCS artifacts attached by start-ticket / ship.

notes.description: Optional free text: slicing rationale, non-goals.
